description.text: Annona was an ancient Italic goddess who embodied the abundance of the yearly harvest. Unlike the more general goddess of abundance, she presided over a single season, personifying the annual crop and often depicted alongside Ceres with sheaves of grain in her hands.

In Roman civic life, the Annona became a state office that evaluated the harvest for taxation and for the creation of reserves to guard against famine. The goddess was also linked to the military annona, a tribute in kind that fed the army, which later evolved into a monetary tax under Diocletian.

curiosities.text: The office of the Annona was responsible for partitioning grain for future sowing and for maintaining a reserve store, making the goddess’s role both sacral and legally binding for farmers.

The military annona, instituted by Emperor Septimius Severus, was originally an exceptional measure to supply the army with grain, but it became a recurring tribute in kind before being replaced by a monetary tax during Diocletian’s reign.
